title: Martin wins red-flagged Norisring Race 2 from seventh on the grid
dek: Maxime Martin won DTM Race 2 at the Norisring for BMW Team RBM, 2.903 seconds ahead of Lucas Auer, after a half-hour red flag for Gary Paffett's heavy crash with Mike Rockenfeller.

chapters.title: BMW's day, Ekström's lead
text: Saturday had belonged to BMW. Bruno Spengler won Race 1 for BMW Team RBM, team-mate Maxime Martin was second and BMW filled five of the top six places, taking its first victory of the 2017 season. Mattias Ekström's third place made him the new championship leader on 77 points, five ahead of René Rast, who had been given a drive-through for crossing the pit-exit line and finished without points. Mercedes had lost Lucas Auer and Robert Wickens on the first lap.

Because every make had run at least one car on wets, the performance weights were left unchanged, so BMW stayed the lightest. Sunday's race brought a mandatory pit stop, and the timing of it was the main strategic choice.

chapters.title: Blomqvist beats Wickens by four thousandths
text: Auer had been quickest in Sunday morning's third practice, and Ekström led the first runs in qualifying with Auer second. Neither improved on their second sets of Hankooks, and in the last minutes pole position changed hands three times within seconds. Spengler lowered Ekström's time, Robert Wickens went quicker still, and then Tom Blomqvist's BMW Team RBM M4 took pole with a 47.252, four thousandths ahead of the Mercedes. Nico Müller then beat Spengler's time to take third in his Audi, so all three makes occupied the front three places.

Spengler lined up fourth, Ekström fifth and Auer sixth. Martin, second on Saturday, could manage only seventh. Mike Rockenfeller was eighth, Timo Glock ninth and Rast tenth, and the whole top ten was quicker than Saturday's pole time. At the other end Loïc Duval was 17th and Maro Engel last, 0.638 seconds off the pace.
Blomqvist came into the session 15th in the standings after a dismal opening to his season, and now had pole for the second race of the weekend.

chapters.title: Wickens leads, Blomqvist slides back and most of the field pits early
text: Wickens made the best start and took the lead, with Blomqvist, on pole, falling to sixth by the end of the first lap. Several cars, Blomqvist and Auer among them, came into the pits at the end of that first lap to take their mandatory stop, and the rest followed, since getting heat into the tyres was the key; by about lap ten most of the field had stopped.

Auer and Martin got their tyres up to temperature quickest and emerged first and second among those who had stopped. Paul di Resta and Edoardo Mortara stayed out longer, and Duval longer still: he was the last to stop, and led on the road until the safety car restart.

chapters.title: Rast and Wickens collide
text: The first interruption came when Wickens and Rast touched on the way out of the Grundig hairpin and both ended up against the wall. Debris brought out the safety car, with Duval, who had not yet been in, leading from Auer and Martin. Duval got away well on the restart, but as he concentrated on defending from Auer, Martin dived up the inside of both to take the lead. Spengler also passed Auer, but Auer got by Duval later on the lap and was promoted back to second when Spengler slowed.
Wickens went on to finish eleventh; Rast did not finish.

chapters.title: Paffett hits the barrier and Rockenfeller
text: On lap 33 the race was stopped. Gary Paffett and Jamie Green touched on the approach to the hairpin; Paffett's Mercedes slammed sideways into the barrier, was thrown back across the track and struck the Audi of Rockenfeller, who was passing through the hairpin. Both drivers climbed out of their cars and were taken to hospital for checks.
The barrier needed repairs and the field waited for about half an hour. The race resumed behind the safety car, with Martin leading Auer, Wittmann, Ekström and Mortara.

chapters.title: Martin holds Auer off, and a photo finish for third
text: Auer made the better start on the restart and went past Martin into the first corner, but Martin stayed in DRS range and took the lead back a few laps later with an inside move at the hairpin. Auer stayed in tow, but he could not retaliate and dropped back in the closing laps, finishing 2.903 seconds behind.

The drama was behind them. Auer spent the closing laps fending off Marco Wittmann. On the penultimate lap Wittmann got a better run out of the hairpin and went to the outside, but had to back off through the Schöller-S, and that let Ekström by for third. On the last lap Wittmann dived for the final hairpin, pushed Ekström wide, and Mortara swept past both of them on the run to the line. Mortara took third by 0.002 seconds from Ekström and 0.027 from Wittmann, giving Mercedes second and third, with Paul di Resta sixth, Augusto Farfus seventh and Jamie Green eighth. Blomqvist, who had started from pole, recovered to ninth.
Martin won from seventh on the grid, and Spengler, who finished twelfth, set the fastest lap. The 66 laps took nearly an hour and a half with the stoppage.

chapters.title: Martin hails a perfect weekend as Ekström and Wittmann clash
text: Martin said he was thrilled. The car had been very good, he said, and the fight with Auer, full of overtakes both ways, had stayed fair. He had been third at the Hungaroring, second on Saturday and now first, and hoped the run would continue. BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt called it a great result for the team and the fans, and noted that the race went down to the last corner. Spengler and Martin had won on successive days for BMW Team RBM, after BMW had gone the first six races of the year without a win.

For Mercedes, after a black Saturday, it was a rollercoaster. Auer finished second despite a cramp in his left foot over the last 20 laps, which made him brake with his right foot, and he said it contributed to a late mistake as Wittmann closed in. Mortara, who said the finish felt like a drag race, had watched the duel between Wittmann and Ekström and was its beneficiary; it was his first podium for Mercedes, and team principal Ulrich Fritz described the outcome as a conciliatory end to a difficult weekend.

Behind the podium, Spengler, Saturday's winner, finished twelfth and Rast and Rockenfeller were out for Audi, which left Ekström as the only Audi driver in the top five. Wittmann was given a warning for pushing Ekström off line, his third of the season, which carries a grid penalty for the first race in Moscow. Audi's Dieter Gass questioned why the sanction was so mild; Ekström said he never files protests, and Wittmann defended himself by saying Ekström had changed direction twice and not committed to a line.

Ekström led the standings with 89 points, two ahead of Auer on 87 and 11 ahead of Martin on 78. Paffett, who apologised to Rockenfeller and thanked the medical staff, escaped with bruising to the collarbone and ribs, while Rockenfeller suffered a small fracture of a metatarsal in his left foot, and his place in Moscow was not yet clear. Roughly 120,000 spectators attended over the weekend. The DTM's next stop is Moscow Raceway, with races on 22 and 23 July.

facts.t: Win from seventh on the grid
facts.v: Maxime Martin won Race 2 over 66 laps in 1:29:22.150, 2.903 seconds ahead of Lucas Auer.

facts.v: Mortara beat Ekström by 0.002 seconds and Wittmann by 0.027 for third place.
Wittmann's third warning of the season for his move on Ekström means a grid penalty for the next round in Moscow.
Ekström led the standings on 89 points, ahead of Auer (87) and Martin (78).
